title: Finite coordinate monomorphisms for affine etale objects after arbitrary base change
statement:
Work in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $v:V\to S$ be etale with $V$ affine, and use the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $\mathcal O_S(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,V)$, which is a sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. There exist an integer $n\geq0$ and sections $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ such that, for every morphism of schemes $a:X\to S$, the map of sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$
$$e_a:h_{X\times_SV}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X^n,\qquad (u:T\to X\times_SV)\longmapsto((\operatorname{pr}_V u)^*c_j)_{j=1}^n$$
is a monomorphism. Here the fibre product is [def-pc-fibre-product] and $h_{X\times_SV}(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,X\times_SV)$. Let $a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\dashv a_{\mathrm{et},*}$ be the inverse and direct image on sheaves of sets and rings [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], with $(a_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal F)(T)=\mathcal F(X\times_ST)$, and let $a^\sharp:a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$ be the adjunct of the map $\mathcal O_S\to a_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_X$ sending $s\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ to $\operatorname{pr}_T^*s\in\Gamma(X\times_ST,\mathcal O)$. Let $\iota_V:a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}h_V\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{X\times_SV}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] normalized as follows: its adjunct $h_V\to a_{\mathrm{et},*}h_{X\times_SV}$ sends $u:T\to V$ to $\mathrm{id}_X\times_Su:X\times_ST\to X\times_SV$. If $e:h_V\to\mathcal O_S^n$ is the map for $a=\mathrm{id}_S$, then $e_a\circ\iota_V=(a^\sharp)^n\circ a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}e$, where $a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(\mathcal O_S^n)=(a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_S)^n$ by finite-limit preservation; in particular $(a^\sharp)^n\circ a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}e$ is a monomorphism. No quasi-compactness or separation condition is imposed on $S$ or $X$.

source.place: Tag 04II (lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S), applied to affine V etale over S; Tag 04IJ (lemma-2-morphism), proof paragraphs 1-2, coordinate injection and its base-change formula; schemes.tex Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion).

proof.text: The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-affine by [lemma-nagata-affine-finite-type-is-quasi-affine], using its first assertion, which has no finite-type hypothesis. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] the etale morphism $v$ is unramified, and by [def-weil-unramified-morphism] an unramified morphism is locally of finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: for every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$, the preimage $v^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ is covered by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra. No assertion that $v$ is quasi-compact over $S$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 04II (lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S), hypotheses; etale implies unramified and hence locally of finite type

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists] to $v$, obtaining $n\geq0$ and an immersion $i:V\to\mathbf A^n_S$ over $S$. By [def-sbc-affine-space], $\mathbf A^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$; let $t_j$ be the pullback of $x_j$ along the second projection and set $c_j=i^*t_j$. For an $S$-scheme $T$, an $S$-map $g:T\to\mathbf A^n_S$ is by [def-pc-fibre-product] the same as a morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ (the compatibility over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is automatic, since $\operatorname{Mor}(T,\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z,\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T))$ is a point by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]), and by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] such a morphism is the same as a ring map $\mathbb Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, i.e. the tuple of images of the $x_j$, which is $(g^*t_j)_j$. So $g\mapsto(g^*t_j)_j$ is injective on $S$-maps $T\to\mathbf A^n_S$. For an $S$-map $w:T\to V$, functoriality of pullback of global functions gives $(iw)^*t_j=w^*c_j$. In particular the tuple $(w^*c_j)_j$ defines a natural transformation $e:h_V\to\mathcal O_S^n$, natural because pullback commutes with composition. The representable presheaf is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 04II (lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S); Tag 04IJ (lemma-2-morphism), first proof paragraph, coordinate injection

proof.text: Write $i=j\circ k$ with $k$ a closed immersion and $j$ an open immersion, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The forward implication of [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes $k$ a monomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] makes $j$ one. Therefore $i$ is left-cancellable: cancel $j$ and then $k$ in any equality $i r=i s$. Fix an arbitrary $a:X\to S$, an etale $T\to X$, and two $X$-maps $u,w:T\to X\times_SV$ with equal displayed coordinate tuples. Their composites $i\operatorname{pr}_V u$ and $i\operatorname{pr}_V w$ are $S$-maps from the same $S$-scheme $T$; their coordinate tuples are $((\operatorname{pr}_Vu)^*c_j)_j=((\operatorname{pr}_Vw)^*c_j)_j$ by step 2, so the injectivity of step 2 (from [def-pc-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]) makes them equal. Cancellation gives $\operatorname{pr}_V u=\operatorname{pr}_V w$. Their $X$-projections are already the given map $T\to X$, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $u=w$. Pullback of functions commutes with restriction, so the maps $e_a$ are morphisms of sheaves (the representable is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]). Each component is injective, hence $e_a$ is a monomorphism: any two sheaf maps equal after $e_a$ are equal at every object and section.

source.place: lemma-immersions-monomorphisms; Tag 04IJ (lemma-2-morphism), first proof paragraph; elementary cancellation in a fibre product replaces invoking Tag 01JY

proof.text:
The normalized representable comparison can be obtained without an arbitrary choice of automorphism. Write $L=a_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ and $R=a_{\mathrm{et},*}$, with the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], and $P=X\times_SV$, which is an object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable]. For every sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, adjunction and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Lh_V,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,RF)\cong (RF)(V)=F(P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_P,F).$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] and invert its isomorphism to obtain $\iota_V:Lh_V\xrightarrow{\sim}h_P$. Under these bijections the identity of $h_P$ corresponds to the identity section of $h_P(P)$, so the adjunct of $\iota_V$ sends $\mathrm{id}_V$ to $\mathrm{id}_P$. Yoneda naturality then says that at $u:T\to V$ it sends $u$ to $\mathrm{id}_X\times_Su$. This is the stipulated normalization.

source.place: Tag 04IJ (lemma-2-morphism), representable comparison in first proof paragraph; Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda), adjunction and Yoneda computation of its normalization

proof.text:
Let $\beta:\mathcal O_S\to R\mathcal O_X$ be the pullback-of-functions map in the statement, whose adjunct is $a^\sharp$. By finite-limit preservation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], $L(\mathcal O_S^n)\cong(L\mathcal O_S)^n$ via the projections, including $n=0$. Compare the two maps $Lh_V\to\mathcal O_X^n$ by the adjunction and then their $j$-th projections. The adjunct of the $j$-th projection of $e_a\iota_V$, evaluated at $u:T\to V$, is
$$ (\operatorname{pr}_V\circ(\mathrm{id}_X\times_Su))^*c_j=(u\circ\operatorname{pr}_T)^*c_j=\operatorname{pr}_T^*(u^*c_j). $$
The adjunct of $a^\sharp\circ L(e_j)$ is $\beta\circ e_j$: explicitly, if $\eta$ is the unit, naturality gives $RL(e_j)\eta_{h_V}=\eta_{\mathcal O_S}e_j$, and $R(a^\sharp)\eta_{\mathcal O_S}=\beta$ is the definition of adjunct. Its value at $u$ is again $\operatorname{pr}_T^*(u^*c_j)$. Thus all projections agree, hence the two product maps agree; for $n=0$ both maps to the terminal sheaf are unique. Finally $e_a$ is monic by step 3 and $\iota_V$ is an isomorphism by step 4, so their composite is monic. The same $n$ and $c_j$ were chosen before $a$, with no condition on $S$ or $X$.
